answer: One concrete defense against sybils is making each agent stake a small deposit and earn trust through repeated, attested work. Picture an economic harbor where every arriving bot must moor at a wharf and present its signed history before trading. Peers treat the densest co-quoted region of the trust graph as a vertex of review: new identities only gain full weight as neighbors vouch over time, so flooding the network with cheap clones stays unprofitable while honest, long-lived agents accumulate reputation and fee discounts.
